docs.title: Web Application Pentesting Methodology
docs.text:
Web application penetration testing is a comprehensive security assessment aimed at identifying vulnerabilities and weaknesses in web applications.

It involves simulating real-world attacks to evaluate the application's security posture and provide recommendations for remediation.

Using a methodology for web application penetration testing is vitally important as it provides a structured and systematic approach to conduct thorough security assessments.

A web application penetration testing methodology helps:

  • Identify potential vulnerabilities and weaknesses
  • Assess the application's security posture
  • Provide actionable recommendations for remediation

docs.title: Popular Methodologies
docs.text: Several web application penetration testing methodologies exist that security professionals can follow. Each has its own approach and focus areas, but all share the common goal of identifying and mitigating security vulnerabilities.

Lab target: DVTA (Damn Vulnerable Thick Client Application)

Note on dnSpy: Use the 32-bit or 64-bit version based on the target application's architecture.

docs.title: Information Gathering
docs.text:
Goals:

  • Explore functionality of the application
  • Identify the architecture
  • Analyze client's network communication
  • Find files accessible by the client
  • Look for sensitive/juicy files

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Tool Purpose CFF Explorer Analyze binary structure and languages used Sysinternals Suite Process monitoring, registry inspection Wireshark Network traffic analysis TCP View Monitor active connections to destination IPs Procmon Process monitoring and file/registry activity

docs.title: TCP View
docs.text: Used to analyze which destination IP addresses the target application connects to.

docs.title: Wireshark
docs.text: Monitor how the application's network traffic flows after authentication and during feature usage.

docs.title: CFF Explorer
docs.text: Analyze the binary to determine what languages/frameworks were used to build it.

docs.title: Procmon (Process Monitor)
docs.text:
Used for process monitoring of the target application.

Filter processes to your target application:

You can also check registry entries by the target application name to look for:

  • Stored credentials
  • Login state (logged in / logged out)
  • Session information
